existing.description: The CERN Research Fellowship Programme, part of CERN's broader Graduate Programme, is an opportunity for recent PhD graduates in physics and engineering to conduct advanced research in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at CERN. It pays a monthly net stipend of either CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 depending on the degree and years of post-graduation experience, together with CERN health insurance for the fellow, their partner and children, a contribution to the CERN Pension Fund, and depending on individual circumstances an installation grant, family, child and infant allowances and travel to Geneva on joining. Fellows receive 30 days of paid leave per year plus two weeks of CERN's annual closure, and on-the-job and formal training including language classes. Contracts run 6 to 24 months with the possibility of extension up to 36 months. Applicants must be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State, must hold a PhD or obtain one within six months, must respect a research-experience cap of six years for Theoretical and Experimental Physics or three years for Applied Sciences and Engineering, and must never previously have held a CERN fellow or graduate contract.
eligibility: National of a CERN Member State or Associate Member State, with a few exceptions possible annually
Applications from Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian and Turkish nationals are currently not considered because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached
For Theoretical and Experimental Physics: PhD completed or obtainable within six months, and no more than 6 years of research experience after the PhD by the application deadline

For Applied Sciences and Engineering: PhD completed or obtainable within six months, and no more than 3 years of research experience after the PhD by the application deadline; candidates with up to 6 years may exceptionally be considered
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before

existing.notes: The official page publishes two stipend tiers, CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 net per month, depending on the candidate's degree and years of post-graduation experience. Because the brief permits only a single number, funding_amount records the lower published tier of 7,004 and the two-tier structure is stated in funding_label and in the notes. This is a paid employment contract with CERN pension and insurance contributions, not a grant, so no tuition component exists or is claimed. CERN's stipends are periodically revised, so the figures should be re-checked against the live page before publication.

existing.description: IMD Business School offers a portfolio of scholarships and need-based bursaries for candidates applying to and entering its one-year full-time MBA in Lausanne. Six named scholarships were listed as open in October 2026: the MBA5 Scholarship of CHF 50,000, the Hilti STEM Scholars Program of CHF 50,000, the Nestle Scholarship for Women of CHF 40,000, the Forté Scholarship for Women of CHF 30,000, IMD MBA Merit Scholarships of up to CHF 40,000, and the BackPack Scholarship for Women with full funding. Most run throughout 2026 on an available-until-allocated basis, while the BackPack Scholarship closes on 14 July. Scholarships are applied for through the Program section of the MBA application form and are awarded to candidates who have applied for and accepted an offer, with selection based on academic and professional excellence, GMAT/GRE scores, career progression, international exposure and Assessment Day performance. Separate need-based bursaries are awarded on proven financial need and confirmed on an ongoing basis.

Bursaries: proven financial need, good academic results, strong reference letter and steady career progression

existing.notes: This record aggregates several distinct awards rather than a single scholarship, so no single funding_amount is reported: the named awards are CHF 50,000 (MBA5, Hilti STEM), CHF 40,000 (Nestle for Women, IMD MBA Merit up to), CHF 30,000 (Forte for Women), and one full-funding award (BackPack for Women). IMD states 48% of students received a scholarship and more than 50% of scholarships are awarded to women. Scholarships require an accepted offer, so they cannot be applied for before admission. The fixed 14 July BackPack date carries no year on the page and has passed relative to 2026-10-04, so no exact deadline is recorded.
